leads.name: Moment
leads.industry: Fintech / wealthtech — 'AI operating system' for investment management (unifies trading, portfolio management, and compliance across asset classes in a single data model)
leads.fundingStage: Series C — $78M closed 2026-05-19, led by Index Ventures with Andreessen Horowitz, Avra, and Lightspeed. Follows a $36M Series B (July 2025). Total raised $134M.
signals: Series C $78M led by Index Ventures announced 2026-05-19; total raised now $134M
Platform now powers investment management for firms managing $10T+ in client assets, up from $300B less than 18 months ago
Named customers: Edward Jones, Hightower, LPL Financial — marquee wealth-management logos
Founded by former quants and traders from Citadel Securities — credible, press-ready founders
Backed by Index Ventures (lead, also led Series B), a16z, Lightspeed — sophisticated investor narrative
'AI OS for investment management' is a clean category-creation story for thought leadership / earned media
leads.source: Daily Scrape 2026-05-21 (Tech Startups VC roundup 2026-05-19; GlobeNewswire; Index Ventures; Finextra; PYMNTS)
leads.notes: Top lead of the day (combined 83, A). Textbook post-raise pr-marketing moment in Mark's exact wheelhouse — NYC fintech/wealthtech with FS buyers, growth stage, a category-defining narrative ('AI OS for investment management'), and an extraordinary proof point ($300B -> $10T client assets in 18 months). Pitch a 90-day comms sprint or a retainer built on the $10T milestone + the Edward Jones / Hightower / LPL logo set + the ex-Citadel founder story. Risk: a $134M-raised company may already have in-house comms or an agency — first-touch should probe for gaps (earned media, exec thought leadership, category PR) rather than assume greenfield. Founders named in coverage are credible spokespeople.

Positioned in the 'agentic productivity' / 'do the work' category — clear narrative angle

leads.notes: Solid B (combined 72). Series A with a marquee angel list that is itself an earned-media hook (Butterfield/Henderson endorsing a Slack-native AI coworker writes its own headline). Pitch a Series-A launch-PR sprint leaning on the angel narrative + the 3,000-integration breadth. Founders not named in coverage; first-touch should ask for marketing lead. Tech (not FS); consumer/prosumer-adjacent productivity, so position carefully for Mark's B2B-finance-leaning brand.

leads.name: Radar
leads.industry: Retail technology / hardware-enabled AI — ceiling-mounted RFID sensor system that tracks store inventory with 99% accuracy for omnichannel retail
leads.fundingStage: Series B — $170M closed 2026-05-19 at a $1B (unicorn) valuation, co-led by Gideon Strategic Partners and Nimble Partners (Align Ventures participating). Total raised $233M+.
signals: Series B $170M at $1B unicorn valuation announced 2026-05-19; total raised $233M+
Named retail customers: Old Navy, American Eagle
99% inventory accuracy vs. industry norm of 65-70% — strong proof data
Dropped BOPIS cancellation rates from 25% to 3%; one pilot reported 60% 'shrink' reduction
Founder/CEO Spencer Hewett named and press-visible
leads.notes: Borderline B (combined 69). Trigger and proof metrics are excellent (unicorn round, named retail logos, hard ROI numbers), but fit is the weak axis: retail/hardware is off Mark's FS/tech center, and a freshly-minted $1B unicorn most likely already runs an in-house comms team or a large agency. Treat as exploratory — a low-cost first outreach to Spencer Hewett to test whether they want incremental retail-trade / vertical storytelling help around the raise. Deprioritize behind Moment / Unframe / Viktor.
